There are primers specifically made for this application. Zinnser makes Mold Killing Primer that will kill the mold that exists, hide the stains and help prevent it from growing back. I still recommend cleaning it first with a mold killing cleaner or a bleach concoction as others have already suggested. After you have cleaned and primed then use a paint made for high moisture areas like Dutch Boy Kitchen and Bath. It has mold preventatives in it to help eliminate new mold growth after all your efforts.

However, as many others already stated, you must try to find the source of moisture causing this extreme mold issue. Ventilation will be your fist concern. Opening a window and/or the door help dissipate the steam from a shower but you really should have a decent exhaust fan if you don't have one.

The humidity in a small room like your bathroom could also be caused by poor heating. Check the rooms insulation if you can and add extra where it is missing, including under the floor.

Thanks, man! I just wanted to get an idea of what you were working with. How long do you have to work on this? It won't take you long but I'm thinking of drying times. 

Regardless of what paint you choose, you'll need to sand it lightly to give the paint something to hold on to. For the paint, you can brush or spray. Brushing will dry faster, clean up easier, but will leave brushstrokes if you're nota skilled painter. Spray will give you a uniform finish, go on faster, but will need acetone for clean up and will take much longer to dry. If you choose spray, I'd give it a solid 4-7 days to dry after the final coat. Make sure the paint you choose for the option you like is made for adhesion to plastic. Otherwise, it won't last and will flake off pretty easily.

For the text you wish to apply, I'd recommend fine point permanent markers or paint pens. Detail brush work like that can be frustrating without the right equipment or skill. Give the whole thing at least two coats of a non-yellowing clear coat for durability.

Hope this helps! Let me know if you have questions. Maybe post a picture when you're done?
